summary.short: Specifies, in 17 Schedules, the descriptions of qualifying entities and UK activities whose acquisitions are notifiable under section 6(2) of the National Security and Investment Act 2021. In force from 4 January 2022 across the UK. Schedule 3 covers artificial intelligence.
summary.long: These Regulations specify, for section 6(2) of the National Security and Investment Act 2021, the descriptions of qualifying entities whose acquisition of control is notifiable. Regulation 2 provides that the Schedules 1 to 17 descriptions apply, and that an entity falls within a description only if it carries on the specified activity in the United Kingdom. Regulation 3 defines development and production. Regulation 4 requires the Secretary of State to review the regulations and publish reports at intervals not exceeding three years, the first before the end of three years from commencement. The Schedules cover advanced materials, advanced robotics, artificial intelligence (research into AI, or developing or producing goods using AI, for identification or tracking of objects, people or events, advanced robotics, or cyber security), civil nuclear, communications (including a turnover condition of at least GBP 50,000,000), computing hardware, critical suppliers to government, cryptographic authentication, data infrastructure, defence, energy (including generating-asset capacity and throughput conditions), military and dual-use, quantum technologies, satellite and space technology, suppliers to emergency services, synthetic biology, and transport (ports and airports). The instrument does not itself set out enforcement penalties or the notification procedure, which sit in the Act.

enforcement.note: This instrument only specifies descriptions of qualifying entities and activities (Schedules 1 to 17) and defines terms (reg. 3). It contains no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension, blocking or other sanctions. It is made under powers in the National Security and Investment Act 2021 (section 6(1), (2), (4) and (8)), which is not part of this text.
